title: Gold Steadies Near Two-Month High as Soft U.S. Data Eases Rate Hike Fears
excerpt: Gold prices hovered near their highest level in more than two months after weak jobs and tame inflation data reduced expectations for near-term Federal Reserve rate hikes.
body:
• Gold prices rallied more than 7% in a week to near $4,400 per ounce, their highest since early June, driven by weak U.S. jobs data and tame inflation readings.
  • U.S. consumer prices cooled to 3.4% in July while producer prices came in flat, reducing market expectations for a Federal Reserve rate hike in September to about 50%.
  • UBS raised its gold price target to $5,000 per ounce for the first half of 2027, citing central bank demand and macroeconomic uncertainty.
  • Geopolitical tensions around Iran and elevated oil prices continue to provide floor support, though a stronger dollar and rising yields capped gains.

Gold prices hovered near a two-month high this week, recovering from intraday dips as a run of soft U.S. economic data eroded expectations for near-term Federal Reserve rate hikes and weakened the dollar.

Spot gold traded around $4,376 per ounce after touching $4,434.84 earlier in the week — its highest level since June 5, according to Reuters. U.S. gold futures settled near $4,441. The precious metal has gained more than 7% over the past week, its strongest weekly advance since January.

Jobs Data Sparked the Rally

The surge began after Friday's U.S. nonfarm payrolls report showed the economy lost 23,000 jobs in July, well below the 80,000 gain economists had forecast and following a downwardly revised increase of just 20,000 in June. The weak print sent gold jumping 2.3% in a single session.

"The weaker-than-expected jobs data presents a scenario where the Fed is going to be less likely to raise interest rates at its next meeting," David Meger, director of metals trading at High Ridge Futures, told Reuters.

The rate futures market repriced quickly. The probability of a Fed rate hike in September dropped to about 44% from 57% before the jobs report, according to LSEG data. By midweek, CME FedWatch showed roughly a 50% chance of a September move and a 79% probability of a hike by December.

Inflation Data Kept the Bid Alive

Subsequent inflation readings reinforced the dovish turn. U.S. consumer prices rose 3.4% year-over-year in July, a modest cooling that eased pressure on the Fed to act aggressively. Producer prices came in flat for the month as energy costs declined, further reducing urgency for tighter monetary policy.

"Gold is still fairly well bid at this point in the wake of last week's jobs data disappointment, which eroded expectations for a rate hike in September."

— Peter Grant, vice president and senior metals strategist at Zaner Metals

Lower interest rates reduce the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding gold, making the metal more attractive relative to bonds and other income-generating assets. The dollar also weakened on the data, making gold cheaper for overseas buyers.

Geopolitical Floor, Yield Ceiling

Geopolitical tensions continued to provide a floor for prices. U.S. President Donald Trump responded to Iran's conditions for a peace deal with his own demands, including compensation for casualties, keeping uncertainty elevated. Oil prices held near a one-week high, sustaining broader commodity market anxiety.

But gains were capped by countervailing forces. The dollar recovered some ground midweek, and Treasury yields remained elevated as markets priced in persistent inflation risks from energy costs. Cleveland Federal Reserve President Beth Hammack said she believed the time was right to begin raising rates gradually to avoid sharper increases later.

Analyst Outlook

Despite the push and pull, the medium-term outlook for gold remains bullish among major banks. UBS raised its gold price target to $5,000 per ounce for the first half of 2027, citing sustained central bank buying and macroeconomic uncertainty.

Central banks added a net 41 metric tons of gold to reserves in May, according to World Gold Council data, underscoring continued institutional demand for the metal as a reserve asset.

Among other precious metals, spot silver traded around $64.80 per ounce after hitting multi-week highs, platinum held near $1,740, and palladium traded around $1,366.

What to Watch

Markets will focus on upcoming Fed commentary and any signals about the September meeting. The interplay between softening U.S. economic data and persistent inflation from energy costs will determine whether gold can break decisively above the $4,400 level or pulls back toward the 100-day moving average near $4,388.
